skill.name: dart-migrate-to-checks-package
skill.description: Migrate Dart tests from package:matcher expect APIs to type-safe package:checks assertions.
skill.summary: Guides reliable migration from Dart matcher assertions to package:checks.
skill.author: dart-lang

security_audit.summary: All 210 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown delimiters and ordinary Dart syntax in documentation. The skill contains no executable scripts, prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or system reconnaissance behavior.

content.user_title: Migrate Dart Tests to Package Checks
content.value_statement: Legacy matcher assertions can lose type safety and hide migration errors. This skill guides precise conversions to package:checks with verification steps and pitfall warnings.
actual_capabilities: Updates Dart test imports for full or incremental package:checks migration.
Maps common matcher assertions to package:checks equivalents.
Handles collection equality, regular expressions, nullable booleans, maps, and extension types.
Explains synchronous and asynchronous exception assertion differences.
Guides conversion of custom Matcher classes into Subject extension methods.
Provides discovery commands and verification steps using Dart analysis and tests.
limitations: It provides migration guidance but does not include an automated codemod.
Project-specific custom matchers still require manual design decisions.
The guidance assumes a Dart package using package:test.
Successful compilation does not guarantee unchanged assertion semantics.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Dart Test Suite
use_cases.description: Convert legacy expect assertions while preserving test intent and improving static type safety.

use_cases.title: Review a Migration Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check conversions for deep equality, asynchronous behavior, nullable values, and matcher-specific pitfalls.

use_cases.title: Replace Custom Matchers
use_cases.description: Redesign custom Matcher subclasses as package:checks Subject extensions with clear rejection messages.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Assertion
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Dart expect assertion to package:checks. Explain any semantic difference and show the required import changes: [assertion]
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is migrating one assertion.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate One Test File
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this Dart test file from package:matcher to package:checks. Preserve behavior, update imports, and identify assertions requiring deep equality: [file content]
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is converting a complete test file.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Partial Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this partial package:checks migration. Find incorrect equality, missing awaits, nullable boolean issues, map containment errors, and remaining legacy expect calls: [changes]
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer is checking migration correctness.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repository Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a staged migration of this Dart repository to package:checks. Group files by risk, address custom matchers, define verification commands, and propose review checkpoints: [repository context]
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer is coordinating a large migration.

output_examples.input: Convert a list equality assertion that currently compares items with an expected list.
output_examples.output: Use deep equality for the migrated collection assertion. Update the test imports, then run static analysis and the focused test.

output_examples.input: Review an asynchronous throwsA migration that chains checks after awaiting throws.
output_examples.output: Use the asynchronous inspection callback because the awaited throws check returns a future. Ensure the assertion itself is awaited.

output_examples.input: Plan conversion of a custom matcher that validates a Person property.
output_examples.output: Create a Subject extension, extract the property with has or nest, and preserve a clear failure description.

best_practices: Migrate one file or coherent test group at a time, then run analysis and focused tests.
Review collection, regular expression, nullable, and asynchronous assertions for semantic differences.
Remove temporary legacy imports only after every expect call has been converted.
anti_patterns: Do not replace every collection expect call with equals without checking deep equality requirements.
Do not omit await from asynchronous checks or assume synchronous throws chaining applies to futures.
Do not remove legacy imports before identifying all remaining matcher dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically edit every Dart test?
faq.answer: No. It guides edits and reviews conversions, but it does not provide a standalone codemod.

faq.question: Can matcher and checks assertions coexist during migration?
faq.answer: Yes. Import package:test scaffolding, package:checks, and the temporary package:test expect library while migrating incrementally.

faq.question: When should I use deepEquals?
faq.answer: Use deepEquals when legacy assertions relied on element-wise comparison of lists, maps, sets, or nested collections.

faq.question: How are asynchronous exception checks different?
faq.answer: Asynchronous throws checks require await and use an inspection callback for additional assertions on the error.

faq.question: Can custom Matcher classes be migrated?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace them with Subject extension methods using the checks context API, has, nest, or asynchronous variants.

faq.question: How should I verify a migration?
faq.answer: Run Dart static analysis, execute focused tests, then run the complete test suite and inspect changed failure messages.
